sentences.text:
This instant application is filed by the petitioner under Section 482 of the Page No.# 2/4 BNSS,
2023 for pre-arrest bail in connection with Vigilance P.S Case No. 13/2025 registered under Section 120B/406/409/420/467/468/471 IPC read with Sections 13(1)(d)/13(2) and 12 of Prevention of Ms Saymeen Mannan vs The State Of Assam on 6 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/17788460/
1 Corruption Act, 1988.
It is the case of the petitioner that she was appointed as Assistant Tourist Information Officer on 19.02.2011 pursuant to a selection process.
She was, thereafter, promoted to the post of Tourist Information Officer on 11.02.2019.
The petitioner, as such, was working since the day of her appointment.

However, on 15.05.2025, an FIR was lodged by the Inspector of Police, Chief Minister's Special Vigilance Cell, Assam stating, inter alia, that the selection process for the post of Assistant Tourist Information Officer in the year 2010 was vitiated on a number of counts.

entities.text: Chief Minister's Special Vigilance Cell, Assam
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: As far as the petitioner is concerned, it was stated therein that in her answer scripts of the written tests, there was over-writing with multiple colored ink in some of the answers.

It was also stated in the FIR that although in the select list, the petitioner was numbered as Sl. No. 4, but she should not have been placed and one another candidate should have been placed on Sl. No. 4.

It was also stated that in place of the petitioner, one another person was deprived and as such, it was directed that criminal case may be registered against the petitioner under the relevant Sections of law.

Mr. G.Z Ahmed, learned counsel for the petitioner submits that there was no proof, as regards the allegation of over-writing on the answer scripts and that the selection was properly held and the petitioner was placed at Sl. No. 4.
He also contends that after so many years, the said FIR, which was at the instance of a complaint filed by one Mr. B.J Sarma, was not warranted at all.

Mr. P Kotoky, learned counsel appearing for Chief Minister's Special Vigilance Cell, Assam submits that the allegations are very serious and that the petitioner Page No.# 3/4 worked illegally in the said post since the day of her appointment and as such, no bail should be granted to the petitioner at this stage.

entities.text: Chief Minister's Special Vigilance Cell, Assam
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: I have heard both the parties at length and on the bare perusal of the FIR as well as other documents which were annexed by the petitioner, it is seen that the petitioner has been working since 2011 and was promoted in 2019 without any blemish and without any complaints, whatsoever.

Although the allegations in this FIR filed on 15.05.2025are very serious, but, since, the length of her service as a Tourist Information Officer was quite long and there was no complain in between, this Court grants her interim bail, only on that count, on furnishing a bond of Rs 25,000/- (Rs Twenty Five Thousand Only) with one surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the Investigating Agency.

The Interim Bail is subject to the following conditions :
(1) She shall co-operate with the Investigating Agency.
(2) She shall appear within 7(seven) days from the receipt of the order before the Investigating Officer for recording her statement.
(3) She shall not leave the territorial jurisdiction without prior permission of the Investigating Agency.
(4) She shall not directly, indirectly make inducement, threats, promiseto any person acquainted with the case.
